notes: NWC construction: computed as (Total current assets minus cash & cash equivalents minus marketable/short-term investments) minus total current liabilities, which includes deferred revenue and operating lease liabilities as part of current liabilities. This produces structurally negative NWC for a SaaS model. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001373715/000137371526000007/now-20251231.htm))

EBIT definition: uses GAAP income from operations as the EBIT proxy (EBIT = income from operations). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001373715/000137371526000007/now-20251231.htm))

D&A and capex: D&A uses cash flow statement line 'Depreciation and amortization' and capex uses cash flow line 'Purchases of property and equipment' (converted from $ in millions to full currency units). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001373715/000137371526000007/now-20251231.htm))

Base-case forecast driver path is an assumption set consistent with observed recent trends (growth deceleration, gradual margin expansion, stable-to-declining D&A and capex intensity) and is not a direct copy of company guidance beyond FY2026. ([investor.servicenow.com](https://investor.servicenow.com/news/news-details/2026/ServiceNow-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-Board-of-Directors-Authorizes-Additional-5B-for-Share-Repurchase-Program/default.aspx))

WACC (0.09) is a modeled input (not directly sourced from filings in this dataset); terminal method is Gordon-growth with terminal_growth = 0.03. ([investor.servicenow.com](https://investor.servicenow.com/news/news-details/2026/ServiceNow-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-Board-of-Directors-Authorizes-Additional-5B-for-Share-Repurchase-Program/default.aspx))

Comps limitation: peer EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA are taken from StockAnalysis.com valuation ratios and treated as NTM proxies (free sources did not clearly provide EV/NTM on the pages captured). Atlassian EV/EBITDA was not available (n/a). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/team/statistics/))

NOL balance is estimated by summing disclosed federal (U.S.), state (approx. $1.0B), Canada, and UK NOL carryforwards; utilization percent (0.80) is an assumption because the filing does not provide a direct utilization factor. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001373715/000137371526000007/now-20251231.htm))

catalysts: Continued conversion of remaining performance obligations (cRPO/RPO) into subscription revenue growth.

Execution against AI-native offerings and workflow monetization (ongoing subscription ARPU/usage expansion). ([investor.servicenow.com](https://investor.servicenow.com/news/news-details/2026/ServiceNow-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-Board-of-Directors-Authorizes-Additional-5B-for-Share-Repurchase-Program/default.aspx))
company_overview: ServiceNow delivers solutions that help organizations govern, secure, and manage AI and digitize and streamline enterprise workflows. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001373715/000137371526000007/now-20251231.htm))

Its core is the cloud-based ServiceNow AI Platform, designed to deliver seamless workflows across departments and personas. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001373715/000137371526000007/now-20251231.htm))
Subscription revenues represented 97% of total revenues in both 2025 and 2024. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001373715/000137371526000007/now-20251231.htm))
current_context: Q4 2025: subscription revenues of $3466 million (+21% YoY) and total revenues of $3568 million (+20.5% YoY). ([investor.servicenow.com](https://investor.servicenow.com/news/news-details/2026/ServiceNow-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-Board-of-Directors-Authorizes-Additional-5B-for-Share-Repurchase-Program/default.aspx))

Full-year 2025: total revenues of $13,278 million (+21% YoY). ([investor.servicenow.com](https://investor.servicenow.com/news/news-details/2026/ServiceNow-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-Board-of-Directors-Authorizes-Additional-5B-for-Share-Repurchase-Program/default.aspx))

FY2026 guidance (full-year): subscription revenues of $15.53-$15.57 billion (+20.5% to 21% YoY), with income from operations margin 32% and free cash flow margin 36%. ([investor.servicenow.com](https://investor.servicenow.com/news/news-details/2026/ServiceNow-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-Board-of-Directors-Authorizes-Additional-5B-for-Share-Repurchase-Program/default.aspx))

Board authorized an additional $5.0 billion share repurchase program (with plans for an imminent $2.0 billion accelerated repurchase). ([investor.servicenow.com](https://investor.servicenow.com/news/news-details/2026/ServiceNow-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-Board-of-Directors-Authorizes-Additional-5B-for-Share-Repurchase-Program/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: Base-case growth decelerates from FY2023-25’s high-20s-to-low-20s trajectory toward mid-teens by FY2030 as the revenue base scales.
EBIT margin expands gradually from FY2023 to FY2025 levels, reflecting operating leverage while maintaining investment for platform and AI roadmap.
Cash conversion is supported by structurally negative working capital tied to deferred revenue dynamics; base-case NWC remains around -0.47 of sales.
Capital intensity stays relatively contained (modeled capex ~6-7% of sales) supporting sustained free cash flow generation.
Tax rate is modeled using the most recent effective tax rate, with NOLs providing a potential incremental tax shield (modeled via NOL utilization).
key_risks: Competitive pricing or platform substitution could slow subscription growth and compress operating leverage.
Cybersecurity/AI reliability or service disruptions can drive customer attrition, costs, and slower renewals.
Working capital dynamics (deferred revenue and associated balances) may diverge from modeled NWC trajectory.
Tax rate variability and limited NOL utilization due to ownership-change rules, jurisdiction mix, or realization uncertainty.

presentation.subtitle: DCF & Comps Input Deck — ServiceNow (NOW)
valuation_summary: DCF uses a Gordon-growth terminal approach with terminal growth of 3% and a modeled WACC of 9% to reflect large-cap SaaS risk and long-run reinvestment needs.
Forecast drivers are anchored to recent GAAP profitability trends (EBIT margin improving from 2023 to 2025) and cash-flow-linked capital intensity.
Comps triangulation uses enterprise software peer EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA plus forward P/E from StockAnalysis.com; EV multiples are treated as NTM proxies due to source limitations.
